intro: The neuter lo: lo de, lo plus adjective plus que, lo mío, and the set phrases built on it.
p.lo cansada que.nota: The adjective agrees with the person or thing, not with lo.
b1.texto:
**Lo** is the neuter article. It never stands before a noun.

- **lo** + adjective makes an idea: **lo bueno**, **lo importante**, **lo mejor**.
- **lo de** + noun, infinitive or adverb points at a matter both speakers know about: ¿sabes **lo de** Ana? Siento **lo de** ayer. **Lo de** trabajar en casa me gusta.
- **lo** + adjective or adverb + **que** means how, with force. The adjective agrees: no sabes **lo cansada que** estoy. Mira **lo bien que** canta. Me sorprende **lo caras que** son.
- **lo** + possessive is my thing, your thing: la cocina no es **lo mío**.
- **lo que** is what.

Set phrases: **a lo mejor**, **por lo menos**, **por lo visto**, **por lo general**, **lo antes posible**, **a lo lejos**.
b3.f0: I'm sorry about yesterday. I shouldn't have shouted.
b3.f1: Don't worry. The important thing is that we've talked about it.
b3.f2: You can't imagine how tired I was.
b3.f3: Apparently, the business of the move has been hard.
b3.f4: Boxes aren't my thing. But look how well the living room has turned out.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Lo que needs a verb after it.
b5.o2.refuerzo: There is no el to join with.
b6.pregunta: Complete: you don't know how expensive they are. (las casas)
b6.o0.refuerzo: The adjective agrees with las casas.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The adjective agrees with what it describes.
b7.pregunta: Complete: the hard part is starting.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Lo plus adjective makes an idea.
b7.o1.refuerzo: El difícil would be the difficult man or thing.
b7.o2.refuerzo: La difícil would be the difficult woman or thing.
b8.o1.explicacion: That would be la cocina no es mía.
b8.o2.explicacion: That would be no tengo cocina.
b9.o1: As you can see, he isn't coming.
b9.o1.explicacion: Por lo visto reports what one has heard.
b9.o2.explicacion: Por lo visto is a fixed phrase: apparently.
b10.traduccion: Look how well the living room has turned out.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a message to a friend about several pending matters without naming them fully: lo de…, lo que…, lo bueno es que…

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Comment aloud on the best, the worst and the strangest thing about the year so far.
b8.o0.explicacion: La cocina no es lo mío means cooking is not my thing or my strength.
b9.o0.explicacion: Por lo visto means apparently, from what people seem to say or see.
